predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Theorem 1.1 (informal) states that TreeCal guarantees calibration error Cal_T^{||·||} ≤ εT for T ≥ (diam(P)/ε)^{O(ρ/ε²)}. However, Corollary C.5 (the formal restatement) states the bound is for T ≥ (diam(P)/ε)^{O(Rate(P,||·||)/ε²)}. The exponent in Theorem 1.1 uses ρ while Corollary C.5 uses Rate(P,||·||). While these are related, they are not identical—ρ is the range of the Bregman divergence while Rate(P,||·||) is defined as the infimum over all such ρ. The informal statement should use Rate(P,||·||) to match the formal version.

In equation (11), the calibration error is written as a sum over labeled pairs (p,σ). The claim states that Cal_T^{||·||²}(x_{1:T}, y_{1:T}) - 2·Cal_T^{||·||²}(x̃_{1:T}, y_{1:T}) ≤ (2·diam(P)²/H²)·T. However, the inequality direction appears reversed. The derivation shows that the left side is bounded above by the right side, but the claim needs this to establish that the calibration error of FTL is close to that of BTL. The inequality should be ≥ not ≤, or the subsequent reasoning needs adjustment.

Theorem 3.1 states that for squared-norm calibration Cal_T^{||·||²} ≤ εT, we need T ≥ (diam(P)/√ε)^{O(ρ/ε)}. This is described as 'singly-exponential dependence on 1/ε'. However, Theorem 1.1 (for non-squared norm) claims T ≥ (diam(P)/ε)^{O(ρ/ε²)}, which is 'doubly-exponential' in 1/ε. The text states 'We arrive at Theorem 1.1 as a corollary of this result by simply applying Cauchy–Schwarz.' But Cauchy-Schwarz (as shown in Corollary C.5) changes √ε to ε in the diameter term, which should only add a factor of 2 to the exponent, not change O(ρ/ε) to O(ρ/ε²). The exponents are inconsistent.

Lemma C.4 claims that Σ_{h=1}^H ||p_h - p̃_h||² ≤ 2·diam(P)². The proof shows ||p̃_h - p_h|| = ||y_h/h - (1/(h(h-1)))Σ_{i=1}^{h-1} y_i||, then claims ||p̃_h - p_h||² ≤ (π²/6)·diam(P)² < 2·diam(P)². However, the bound (π²/6) ≈ 1.645 appears without justification. The expression ||y_h/h - (1/(h(h-1)))Σ y_i|| does not obviously lead to this specific constant. The derivation of this bound is missing or incorrect.

predicted_errors.error_location: Theorem 4.3 vs Theorem D.2 lower bound exponents
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Theorem 4.3 states a lower bound requiring T ≥ exp(Ω(min{d^{1/7}, ε^{-1/6}})) for ℓ₁ calibration. However, the theorem statement says 'T ≤ exp(c·min{d^{1/14}, ε^{-1/6}})' with exponent 1/14 on d. Similarly, Theorem D.2 for ℓ₂ calibration uses min{d^{1/14}, ε^{-1/7}}. The abstract and introduction claim the lower bound is exp(Ω(1/ε)), but the formal statements have ε^{-1/6} or ε^{-1/7}, which are weaker. This inconsistency suggests either the informal claims are overstated or the formal bounds have errors.
